title: Data Structures
description: Fundamental computer science data structures with their average-case time complexities.

results.name: Array
results.description: A contiguous block of memory storing elements of the same type, indexed by position.

results.name: Dynamic Array
results.description: A resizable array that grows automatically; amortized O(1) append by doubling capacity.

results.name: Singly Linked List
results.description: A sequence of nodes where each node points to the next; insertion at a known position is constant.

results.name: Doubly Linked List
results.description: A linked list whose nodes point both to the next and previous nodes, allowing bidirectional traversal.

results.name: Stack
results.description: A last-in, first-out (LIFO) collection supporting push and pop at one end.

results.name: Queue
results.description: A first-in, first-out (FIFO) collection with enqueue at the rear and dequeue at the front.

results.name: Deque
results.description: A double-ended queue allowing constant-time insertion and removal at both ends.

results.name: Hash Table
results.description: Maps keys to values using a hash function; average constant-time lookup and insertion.

results.name: Hash Set
results.description: A collection of unique elements backed by a hash table for fast membership testing.

results.name: Binary Search Tree
results.description: A binary tree where each node's left subtree is smaller and right subtree is larger than the node.

results.name: AVL Tree
results.description: A self-balancing binary search tree that keeps subtree heights within one, guaranteeing log-time operations.

results.name: Red-Black Tree
results.description: A self-balancing binary search tree using node colors to maintain balance during insertion and deletion.

results.name: B-Tree
results.description: A self-balancing multi-way tree that keeps data sorted for efficient disk-based storage and databases.

results.name: Trie
results.description: A prefix tree storing strings by character, where k is the length of the key being searched or inserted.

results.name: Binary Heap
results.description: A complete binary tree satisfying the heap property; the min or max element is always at the root.

results.name: Fibonacci Heap
results.description: A heap with amortized constant-time insert and decrease-key, used in advanced graph algorithms.

results.name: Priority Queue
results.description: An abstract queue where each element has a priority and the highest-priority element is served first.

results.name: Adjacency List
results.description: A graph representation storing, for each vertex, a list of its adjacent vertices; space-efficient for sparse graphs.

results.name: Adjacency Matrix
results.description: A graph representation using a V-by-V matrix where each cell marks whether an edge exists between two vertices.

results.name: Skip List
results.description: A layered linked list with express lanes that allow probabilistic logarithmic search and insertion.
